findings.summary: Frozen checked-in synthetic Source artifacts now carry verified SHA-256 bindings, and every reviewed supporting EvidenceLink reproducibly binds its unique locator to the revision's exact source-native raw expression and atomic Claim statement.

The #330 temporal envelope is representable, but refinement does not preserve it fail-closed: full-package adversarial validation accepted a spatial refine whose bounds stayed equal while start_inclusive changed from true to false and start_qualifier changed from approximate to not_before. Calendar, inclusivity, qualifiers and alternatives are not compared as part of valid-time equality/subset semantics, so an unrelated dimension refinement can silently alter or discard material temporal meaning.

The validator rejects multiple series for one atomic (subject_ref,target_key), enforces target-key/dimension compatibility, and validates each revision value family against the declared series dimension.

Valid time and record time remain distinct; deterministic replay, correction, alternatives, withdrawal, world-state separation, fuzzy ranges and geometry-null unknown routes preserve the intended semantic scenarios.

The intake/promotion chain, material-fidelity stop rule, Gate D and public-runtime boundaries, empty Airtable historical-write boundary, and frozen #329/#330/Gate C packages remain explicitly preserved.

conclusion: Remote PR head, frozen tree and reviewed-content digest are verified; the validator, 35 focused tests and release check pass. REF-SEM-001 and REF-SEM-003 are resolved, but REF-SEM-002 remains materially open because unrelated-dimension refinement can silently change accepted #330 temporal-envelope semantics.
